case.title: 비트코인 채굴기와 솔로 마이닝 가이드
case.summary: 데스크톱 비트코인 채굴기의 제품 소개, 채굴 원리, 설정 방법과 일상적인 사용을 다룹니다. 시연에는 주로 Bitaxe Gamma 601이 사용됩니다. 주제별로 영상을 살펴보고 원본 파일, 제공되는 자막과 관련 자료를 확인할 수 있습니다.
case.historical: 이전 작품은 제작 당시의 버전으로 보존합니다. 사양, 가격, 보상은 달라질 수 있습니다.
case.caveat: 솔로 마이닝은 보상을 보장하지 않습니다. 원본 영상의 제품 정보와 StarMiner 표기는 유지됩니다.

creator100-c001: Why can an accepted share still not be a Bitcoin block?

A pool can accept work that meets its share target. The network checks a separate, harder target, plus the other block rules. So an accepted share is not proof of a new Bitcoin block. English educational edition with manufacturer imagery and labeled illustrations.
creator100-c002: Who actually sends a miner its next job?

The hashing hardware does not invent the whole job by itself. Mining software constructs work from a block template; a pool can provide that work. The hardware tries candidate headers and sends results back. English educational edition with manufacturer imagery and labeled illustrations.
creator100-c003: What happens when a miner runs out of nonce values?

The header nonce has a finite range of possible values. Mining software can change extra data in the coinbase transaction. That changes the Merkle root and creates a different header to try. English educational edition with manufacturer imagery and labeled illustrations.
creator100-c004: Does everyone have exactly the same waiting transactions?

A mempool is a node's local collection of unconfirmed transactions. Nodes can hear transactions at different times and use different acceptance policies. Two waiting lists can differ without there being two different Bitcoin systems. English educational edition with manufacturer imagery and labeled illustrations.
creator100-c005: Does a miner sign your transaction for you?

A wallet prepares the spending authorization for a transaction. Mining software can include valid transactions in a candidate block. Including your transaction does not mean signing it on your behalf. English educational edition with manufacturer imagery and labeled illustrations.
creator100-c006: Where does a wallet balance come from?

A wallet's balance can come from several unspent transaction outputs. Each output is a separate piece that can later be spent. The displayed total is a summary, not one digital coin sitting in a drawer. English educational edition with manufacturer imagery and labeled illustrations.
creator100-c007: Does a coinbase transaction mean the exchange?

In the protocol, a coinbase transaction is the special first transaction in a block. It can create the permitted block subsidy and collect transaction fees. That protocol term is separate from a company with the same name. English educational edition with manufacturer imagery and labeled illustrations.
creator100-c008: Can a newly created block reward be spent immediately?

A coinbase output has a maturity rule before it can be spent. Seeing an output in a block is different from being allowed to spend it. The protocol checks that condition; a screen cannot override it. English educational edition with manufacturer imagery and labeled illustrations.
creator100-c009: Why can a larger transaction need a different fee?

Transaction fees are often discussed as a rate per virtual byte. Data weight and payment value are different things. A larger payment does not automatically mean a heavier transaction. English educational edition with manufacturer imagery and labeled illustrations.
creator100-c010: Why does one payment sometimes create more than one output?

A transaction can spend an output and create several new outputs. One can go to the recipient, while another returns change to the sender. The remaining difference can be the fee; these are abstract pieces, not real funds. English educational edition with manufacturer imagery and labeled illustrations.
creator100-c011: Can you check one transaction without carrying the whole block?

A Merkle path combines one transaction hash with the necessary sibling hashes. The result can be checked against the root in a block header. That proves inclusion relative to that root, not that every other block rule is valid. English educational edition with manufacturer imagery and labeled illustrations.
creator100-c012: Does mining hardware hash every transaction on each attempt?

Bitcoin proof of work hashes the block header. The full transaction list is tied to that header through its Merkle root. A new attempt does not mean reading every transaction all over again. English educational edition with manufacturer imagery and labeled illustrations.
creator100-c013: Who chooses the transactions in a candidate block?

A block template can suggest transactions to mining software. The software assembles candidate contents under the relevant rules. Trying hashes and choosing those contents are different jobs; arrangements vary. English educational edition with manufacturer imagery and labeled illustrations.
creator100-c014: Is a mining job a coin, a file, or a message?

In classic Stratum, the pool sends structured messages about mining work. Those messages provide fields needed to construct candidate headers. A job message is not a coin arriving in a wallet. English educational edition with manufacturer imagery and labeled illustrations.
creator100-c015: Is there only one exact hash a miner must find?

The proof of work check compares a hash value with a target. A value that does not exceed the target passes that particular check. It does not need to match one unique secret string; other block rules still apply. English educational edition with manufacturer imagery and labeled illustrations.
creator100-c016: Can you validate a proof just by counting leading zeros?

Leading zeros can help draw the idea of a small hash value. But counting those zeros alone does not perform the full target comparison. Values can share a prefix and still fall on different sides of a target. English educational edition with manufacturer imagery and labeled illustrations.
creator100-c017: Can we demonstrate a block without pretending it happened on Bitcoin?

Regtest provides a separate environment for controlled Bitcoin experiments. A block in that sandbox is not a block on the public Bitcoin network. This animation only illustrates the separation; no node or live miner is running here. English educational edition with manufacturer imagery and labeled illustrations.
creator100-c018: Does every mining gadget need to store the whole blockchain?

Storing and validating chain data is one role. Trying candidate headers for proof of work is another. In a common setup, software and hashing hardware divide those tasks. English educational edition with manufacturer imagery and labeled illustrations.
creator100-c019: What information can receive bitcoin without spending it?

A receiving address lets someone direct a payment to a destination. A private key is a secret used to authorize spending. These have different roles; no real address or secret appears in this diagram. English educational edition with manufacturer imagery and labeled illustrations.
creator100-c020: Can a share target and a network target mean different things?

A pool's share target checks submitted work for its own accounting. Bitcoin's network target is a separate proof of work condition. A share can meet one without meeting the other; neither is a payment receipt. English educational edition with manufacturer imagery and labeled illustrations.
